newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Senate rejects motion on CVRD.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Senate rejects motion on CVRD.

text.p: The Brazilian government crushed a bid by left-wing opposition parties to speed up progress on a bill that would make the privatization of mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) subject to Congressional approval.

In a latest setback for opponents of the upcoming CVRD sell-off, the government defeated by 43-23 votes in the Senate a motion which would have enabled the bill to be put to a vote on the floor of the Senate next week.

The bill, which seeks to give the Senate powers to veto the tender details relating to the privatization, now faces several committee stages and is unlikely to be approved before the sale of a 40-45 block of CVRD voting shares, slated for April.

Left-wing parties have unsuccessfully floated several bills in the Senate in an attempt to give the upper house powers over what is set to become South America's biggest-ever privatization, with receipts expected to total about $6.0 billion.
Tender documents relating to the block sale may be published Friday or next week.
